name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on enhancing police cooperation in relation to the prevention, detection and investigation of migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, and on enhancing Europol’s support to preventing and combating such crimes and amending Regulation (EU) 2016/794
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on a new law to fight migrant smuggling and human trafficking. It keeps the plan to create a European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling inside Europol, the European Union's police agency, and adds it into Europol's existing rulebook instead of a separate law. It asks Member States to share more information with Europol, lets Europol process biometric data under strict safeguards, and adds 50 staff posts.

- A new Europol centre coordinates police work against smuggling and trafficking; Member States share more data.
- It affects Europol, national police and border agencies, Eurojust and the border agency Frontex.
- Parliament negotiates the final text with EU governments; the law is not yet in force.
